Title: ilha: Your Claude Code and Codex limits, live in the notch | Product Hunt
# ilha. ## Your Claude Code and Codex limits, live in the notch. ilha is a native Mac app that lives in the notch (a small pill on other displays) and shows how much of your Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build limits you've used: the 5-hour and weekly windows, when they reset, and whether you're on pace to run out. If you pay for several accounts, it switches the CLI to one with room before the limit, without logging anything out. Insights prices each week at API rates, by project. Launch tags:Mac•Developer Tools•Artificial Intelligence. I use Claude Code and Codex all day, with a few accounts each, and I kept finding out I was out of room mid-task, then logging out and guessing which account still had some. ilha sits in the notch and shows each account's 5-hour and weekly windows. When one runs low it offers to switch, and at the limit it switches for you, swapping the CLI's login in place, so nothing gets logged out and running Claude Code sessions carry on. It reads the usage straight from Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI with the logins already on your Mac, and nothing about your usage, logins or logs ever leaves it. Free covers one account per CLI; Pro is $20 once (a year of updates) for every account, switching and Insights, with 14 days to try it, no account needed. I'd love to hear what you'd want it to show next.

Claude's limits are rolling windows, so 78% tells me nothing until I know whether the window resets in eight minutes or four hours, and that's the actual decision I'm making at that moment, start the big refactor or go make coffee. since this is unofficial and there's no cloud account, I'm guessing it's reading local session/config files or an undocumented local endpoint rather than a published usage API from Anthropic or Cursor. From what's described, the split seems to be usage visibility vs session monitoring: this shows you how much quota you have left, BlackFlare tells you when a running session finishes or gets stuck and keeps your Mac awake while it runs. Hey everyone, I built Code Meter because I kept getting blindsided by Claude Code rate limits in the middle of deep coding sessions. Checking /usage for claude or going on the Minimax api page to check for usage, felt wrong, so I built the thing I wanted: a tiny menu bar app that shows your usage percentage at all times. A few things I’m proud of:. It doesn’t just show your current percentage. It tells you whether you’re on pace to hit the limit, and roughly when. I keep a small widget on my desktop so I can see my usage without even clicking the menu bar icon. When your usage is stable, it polls less often. When things are moving, it speeds up. Keeps the data fresh without hammering the API. If you use Minimax’s Token Plan for coding, Code Meter tracks that too. Just paste your API key. It’s a native macOS app. SwiftUI, Liquid Glass, no Electron. Runs in the menu bar with no dock icon. Feels like it belongs on your Mac because it does. I’d love to hear what you think and what features you’d want next. Happy to answer any questions.
